assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demand estimation with endogenous prices and product characteristics in differentiated-product markets, plus tractable dynamic industry models, changed empirical industrial organisation. The methods are now standard in merger review, antitrust and regulatory practice, and they give a transferable way to connect structural theory with data.
assessment.attribution: The core demand-side contribution is most clearly Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes, with Pakes also central to dynamic models and estimation. Bresnahan, Benkard, Reiss and Levin made real contributions, but the three-laureate limit makes the demand-estimation core the cleanest credit set. Some contribution-credit trade-offs are unavoidable.
assessment.maturity: The foundational work dates from the 1990s and has been confirmed over decades through wide adoption and extensive methodological refinement. Timing is not a concern.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee would prefer a broader empirical-IO prize that includes Bresnahan.
How to weigh the demand-estimation core against dynamic-model contributions when the credit set is limited to three.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Political economics formalised how constitutions, electoral rules and political institutions shape fiscal policy, state capacity and economic outcomes. It built a coherent theoretical and empirical research programme, and it links to the institutions-and-prosperity agenda recognised in 2024 while covering different ground (policy choice under electoral and constitutional rules).
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the central pair through their theory and empirical work on constitutions and policy. Besley's contributions on state capacity and political agency are substantial and complementary. A Persson link to Committee history is disclosed here but not adjudicated. Other contributors could argue for credit.
assessment.maturity: The field has developed since the 1990s, with a book-length synthesis and a large body of follow-on work, and it is well confirmed by now.
uncertainties: Causal identification on constitutional effects is harder than for natural-experiment settings, and some empirical findings remain debated.
Overlap with the 2024 prize may make the Committee wary of recognising institutions again soon.
Disclosed conflicts or proximity to Persson are noted and not resolved here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints generate credit cycles in which small shocks are amplified and persist. This is a core mechanism in macro-finance, and it is the standard framework for understanding financial frictions and the transmission of asset-price movements to real activity, with direct relevance after the 2008 crisis.
assessment.attribution: The 1997 Kiyotaki–Moore model is the clear, identifiable origin. Gertler and Gilchrist belong to the related financial-accelerator literature built on Bernanke's earlier work, so including them blurs attribution. The two-person set is cleaner.
assessment.maturity: The model is nearly three decades old and thoroughly absorbed into macro teaching and policy modelling. It is mature.
uncertainties: Credit division with the Bernanke–Gertler financial accelerator strand.
Empirical validation relies largely on later work by others.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-firm trade models explain exporter selection, intra-industry reallocation and new channels for gains from trade, shifting the field's focus from industries to firms. The framework is widely used both in theory and in empirical work using firm-level data.
assessment.attribution: Melitz's 2003 model is the pivotal contribution. Helpman's work on trade with firm heterogeneity and on new trade theory gives broad support. Redding's contributions are extensive in quantitative and spatial trade but add to the credit spread. Bernard, Eaton and Kortum are important contributors who are not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of confirmation, with thousands of applications and a large amount of follow-on work. Mature.
uncertainties: Omission of Bernard, Eaton and Kortum from this candidate's credited names affects fair attribution.
Trade-theory prizes depend on how the Committee weighs this against the Krugman-era new trade theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities underpins the contemporary theory and practice of monetary policy, including inflation targeting and policy rules. Its influence on central banks is large.
assessment.attribution: Credit is highly diffuse across Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets. A three-person selection is necessarily arbitrary and risks omitting essential contributors. Woodford (synthesis and normative theory), Gali (empirical and analytical implementation) and Taylor (rule and staggered contracts) is one defensible set.
assessment.maturity: Developed over three to four decades and well confirmed in practice, although the post-2008 and post-2021 inflation experiences have prompted reassessment.
uncertainties: Attribution difficulty and the risk of an incomplete credit set.
Debate over how well the framework performed in recent episodes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data have made it possible to measure intergenerational mobility and its geographic variation, including causal evidence on neighbourhood effects. The work has had major scientific and policy influence and changed how mobility is studied.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear leader. Hendren's contributions on place effects and causal neighbourhood estimates are substantial. Friedman and Katz are significant co-authors. Chetty's credit across several lines (this and the tax candidate) complicates attribution.
assessment.maturity: The central results are about a decade old, and replication and follow-up are ongoing. This is somewhat early compared with older candidates, though influence has been quick.
uncertainties: The final credit set and the relative roles of the Opportunity Insights collaborators.
Robustness of some place-effect estimates and their long-run durability.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-run top-income and wealth series built from tax records revived the empirical study of distribution and shaped public debate and research agendas. The data infrastructure (World Inequality Database) is a durable contribution.
assessment.attribution: The three are well matched to the data contribution (Piketty–Saez on top incomes, Zucman on wealth and offshore holdings). The theoretical content is less novel than the measurement, and Piketty's interpretive claims about r > g have been contested.
assessment.maturity: The top-income work is two decades old and widely confirmed in broad outline, while the wealth and offshore estimates are more recent and debated.
uncertainties: Methodological disputes about wealth-capitalisation and offshore estimates.
Whether measurement and data work of this sort meets the Committee's threshold when conceptual novelty is limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework quantifies how distortions in resource allocation across firms account for cross-country TFP gaps. It gave growth and development economics a measurable mechanism and a widely used empirical methodology.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow's 2009 paper is the key reference, and Restuccia and Rogerson's related work is a close parallel, so attribution to Restuccia is arguable. Restuccia is also credited here and might have a claim equal to Klenow's.
assessment.maturity: About 17 years of confirmation and extensions, with substantial use in policy analysis. Reasonably mature, though measurement sensitivity is a known concern.
uncertainties: Sensitivity of the results to measurement error and assumptions about markups and adjustment costs.
Credit division with Restuccia and Rogerson, who is not on the credited list.
